          ADDM Report for Task 'ADDM:2600903132_1_31232'
          ----------------------------------------------

Analysis Period
---------------
AWR snapshot range from 31231 to 31232.
Time period starts at 06-APR-26 11.30.07 AM
Time period ends at 06-APR-26 12.30.37 PM

Analysis Target
---------------
Database 'ARYABHAT' with DB ID 2600903132.
Database version during analysis period was 19.29.0.0.0.
Database version when ADDM was executed was 19.0.0.0.0.
All recommendations generated by ADDM are valid for database version 19.0.0.0.0, the version in which ADDM was executed.
ADDM performed an analysis of instance aryabhat, numbered 1 and hosted at
ambaddb1.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 33361 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 9.19.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
   Description                         Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                       Percent of Activity
   ----------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1  Session Connect and Disconnect      1.69 | 18.42         1
2  Undersized SGA                      1.16 | 12.65         1
3  Soft Parse                          1.1 | 11.92          2
4  Hard Parse Due to Invalidations     .73 | 7.97           1

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.69 active sessions, 18.42% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.69 active sessions, 18.42% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Undersized SGA
Impact is 1.16 active sessions, 12.65% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "143360 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1 active sessions, 10.89% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      188160 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.29 active sessions, 14.07% of total activity.
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.1 active sessions, 11.92% of total activity.


Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.1 active sessions, 11.92% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.1 active sessions, 11.92% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.1 active sessions, 11.92% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 4: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .73 active sessions, 7.97% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .73 active sessions, 7.97% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.1 active sessions, 11.92% of total activity.


Finding 5: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .59 active sessions, 6.38% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .32 active sessions, 3.46% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 7% for SQL execution,
      26% for parsing, 67% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .27 active sessions, 2.92% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the INSERT statement with SQL_ID
      "gvhbumfb6gsw3".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID gvhbumfb6gsw3.

Finding 6: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is .54 active sessions, 5.84% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .54 active sessions, 5.84% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 22 K and the
      average time per write was 0 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 9.3 M per second for
      reads and 19 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 67% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 32% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .54 active sessions, 5.84% of total activity.


Finding 7: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria

Impact is 1.2 active sessions, 15.19% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.2 active sessions, 15.19% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is .98 active sessions, 12.36% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .98 active sessions, 12.36% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .98 active sessions, 12.36% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 4: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .59 active sessions, 7.51% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------

additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis

   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.
